title: Type 2 diabetes: outpatient management (India, RSSDI)
subject: endocrinology
setting: Primary care, NCD clinic, diabetes clinic
summary: Diagnose with FPG 126 mg/dL, 2-hour OGTT glucose 200 mg/dL or HbA1c 6.5% or more. Start lifestyle therapy and metformin at diagnosis, escalate by HbA1c (dual therapy, then a third agent or basal insulin), prefer SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 RAs with ASCVD, heart failure or kidney disease, and aim for HbA1c below 7%, BP below 130/80 and LDL-C below 100 mg/dL.

sections.title: Screen and diagnose
items: Diabetes: fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or more, 2-hour plasma glucose on 75 g OGTT 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more, HbA1c 6.5% or more, or random glucose 200 mg/dL or more with classic symptoms. Repeat an abnormal test in an asymptomatic person unless unequivocal.

Prediabetes (RSSDI): impaired fasting glucose 110 to 125 mg/dL (6.1 to 6.9 mmol/L), impaired glucose tolerance 140 to 199 mg/dL (7.8 to 11.0 mmol/L) on OGTT, or HbA1c 5.7 to 6.4%. The ICMR STW uses 100 to 125 mg/dL for IFG.
Fasting glucose alone misses many Indians with diabetes: use an OGTT where possible. Exclude anaemia before relying on HbA1c.

Screen opportunistically: people attending for unrelated illness, family members of people with diabetes, antenatal and dental patients, overweight children at puberty. ICMR: adults over 30, or BMI 23 kg/m2 or more with a risk factor (family history, CVD, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, inactivity, PCOS, acanthosis, previous GDM).
Also test adults with osmotic symptoms, unexplained weight loss, ACS, deep-seated or recurrent infections (liver abscess, TB, pyelonephritis, carbuncle, candidiasis) or non-healing foot ulcers.
Classify by WHO: type 1, type 2, hybrid forms (slowly evolving immune-mediated diabetes of adults, ketosis-prone type 2), other specific types, and hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy.

sections.title: Baseline assessment
items: Weight, BMI, waist, BP, peripheral pulses, foot, skin and oral examination, and dilated fundus examination at diagnosis.
HbA1c, creatinine with eGFR (CKD-EPI), potassium, fasting lipid profile, urine routine and spot urine albumin to creatinine ratio, liver enzymes, and ECG.
Estimate cardiovascular risk and record current or previous CVD events at the first and later visits.

sections.title: Lifestyle and medical nutrition therapy (all patients)
items: Carbohydrate 50 to 60% of calories, mainly complex and low-glycaemic-index; limit white rice (prefer brown rice or millets); fibre 25 to 40 g a day. Protein about 15% of calories; fat below 30% with saturated fat below 10% (below 7% if triglycerides are high).

Vegetables and fruit should make up half the plate; rotate 2 or more vegetable oils; avoid vanaspati, reheated or refried oil, fried street food, sugar-sweetened drinks and late dinners. Salt below 5 g a day (sodium below 2300 mg).

At least 150 minutes a week of physical activity, ideally 30 minutes or more of moderate aerobic activity daily, plus muscle-strengthening at least 3 times a week and at least 5000 steps a day. Yoga helps but should not replace aerobic exercise.
Stop tobacco and avoid alcohol. Behavioural counselling and diabetes self-management education at diagnosis and every visit.

Prediabetes: lose 5 to 10% of weight if overweight, activity 30 minutes a day (1 hour if obese), 6 to 8 hours sleep. If no benefit after 6 months, add metformin 500 mg twice daily in younger overweight people with IFG plus IGT or IFG plus HbA1c above 5.7%; an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor if metformin is not tolerated.

sections.title: Glucose-lowering drugs: stepwise
items: Start metformin with lifestyle measures at diagnosis. If metformin is contraindicated: sulfonylurea (or glinide), pioglitazone, DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT2 inhibitor, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor or oral semaglutide.

ICMR starting guide by HbA1c: below 8.5% metformin alone; 8.5 to 10% metformin plus a second agent (sulfonylurea, pioglitazone, DPP-4 inhibitor, SGLT2 inhibitor, AGI or GLP-1 RA); above 10% basal insulin plus metformin plus another oral drug, or triple oral therapy.
Not at target: add a second, then a third agent chosen by patient profile (age, BMI, kidney disease, duration, CVD, cost, glycaemic pattern, hypoglycaemia risk).
Established or high risk of ASCVD, heart failure, diabetic kidney disease, or need for weight loss: prefer an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven cardiovascular benefit.

Elderly or high hypoglycaemia risk: a DPP-4 inhibitor rather than a sulfonylurea. Prominent post-meal peaks: AGI, glinide or SGLT2 inhibitor. In resource-limited care metformin, newer sulfonylureas and pioglitazone are acceptable.
Insulin: when targets are not met on 3 oral agents, or at presentation with severe symptomatic hyperglycaemia or an unstable state.

sections.title: Insulin: initiate, titrate, intensify
items: Initiate once-daily basal insulin, once-daily premix or co-formulation, or twice-daily premix, with matched meal timing, and teach SMBG and hypoglycaemia recognition.
Self-titrate by 2 to 4 units weekly or every 2 weeks, fixing fasting glucose first and then post-meal values.
Titration goals: pre-meal glucose below 115 mg/dL (6.4 mmol/L) and 2-hour post-meal below 160 mg/dL (8.9 mmol/L); if at high risk of hypoglycaemia, below 130 and 180 mg/dL.

If still above goal after optimal titration: premix twice or three times daily, a co-formulation regimen, basal plus prandial insulin with the largest meal (progressing to basal-bolus), or add a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

sections.title: Targets and monitoring
items: ABC targets: HbA1c below 7%, BP below 130/80 mmHg (below 140/80 in the elderly), LDL-C below 100 mg/dL. Post-meal glucose target 160 mg/dL provided hypoglycaemia is avoided. Relax the HbA1c target after unacceptable hypoglycaemia; tighten it only if achieved safely.
HbA1c every 3 to 6 months; change treatment if above the agreed target on 2 consecutive occasions. SMBG for everyone on insulin, sulfonylureas or glinides.

Kidneys at diagnosis and yearly: urine albumin to creatinine ratio and eGFR. If ACR is above 30 mg/g, repeat twice over 4 months; confirmed if 2 of 3 are raised. ACR above 300 mg/g is macroalbuminuria.
Eyes at diagnosis, then every 1 to 2 years if no retinopathy (the ICMR STW advises yearly), 12-monthly with minimal stable retinopathy, 3 to 6 monthly if worsening, and more often in pregnancy.
Annual foot review with monofilament, vibration and pulses; never walk barefoot. Assess neuropathy and autonomic symptoms; baseline and yearly liver enzymes for NAFLD; ECG yearly.
Statin if LDL-C is above 70 mg/dL with target organ damage or above 100 mg/dL in uncomplicated diabetes; low-dose aspirin in high-risk patients. Annual influenza vaccine.

sections.title: Kidney disease, hypertension, elderly and remission
items: Diabetic kidney disease: prefer an SGLT2 inhibitor; ACEI or ARB titrated to maximum tolerated dose for any albuminuria; monitor ACR, eGFR and potassium; limit protein to 0.8 g/kg/day in advancing CKD. Refer if eGFR is below 30, kidney function falls rapidly, or features suggest non-diabetic disease (onset under 5 years, no retinopathy, active urine sediment).
Hypertension with diabetes: ACEI or ARB first line, especially with albuminuria; add a CCB and/or thiazide-like diuretic (see the API-ICP protocol).

Elderly: start low, go slow; metformin first line; DPP-4 inhibitors are weight neutral with low hypoglycaemia risk; SGLT2 inhibitors are suggested up to about 70 years; screen for cognitive impairment and frailty.
Remission: HbA1c below 6.5% persisting for at least 3 months without glucose-lowering drugs; recheck yearly. Bariatric surgery gives the most consistent remission in obese patients.

sections.title: Hypoglycaemia
items: Alert value below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L); clinically significant below 54 mg/dL (3.0 mmol/L). Warn every patient on insulin, sulfonylureas or glinides.
Conscious: oral glucose 15 to 20 g, recheck after 15 minutes and repeat if still low, then a meal or snack.
Unconscious or severe: IV glucose or IM glucagon; repeat glucagon 0.5 mg IM or SC if there is no improvement.
Recurrent episodes: revise the regimen; prefer newer sulfonylureas or modern insulins in those at high risk.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Relying on fasting glucose alone and missing post-load hyperglycaemia common in Indians.
Clinical inertia: leaving HbA1c above target for 2 or more visits without changing therapy.
Delaying insulin in a symptomatic patient with very high glucose or weight loss.
Not using SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 RAs in patients with heart failure, ASCVD or kidney disease.
Skipping yearly ACR, eye and foot checks.

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.dose: First line from diagnosis; RSSDI dose for prediabetes is 500 mg orally twice daily
drugs.notes: Stop the night before surgery; do not restart if renal function is impaired.

drugs.name: Basal, premix or co-formulation insulin
drugs.dose: Once daily basal (or once or twice daily premix); titrate by 2 to 4 units weekly or every 2 weeks to pre-meal glucose below 115 mg/dL
drugs.notes: Use higher goals (below 130 and 180 mg/dL) if hypoglycaemia risk is high.

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitor
drugs.dose: Add-on or first choice with ASCVD, heart failure or DKD
drugs.notes: Genital infections; ketoacidosis risk. RSSDI suggests use up to about 70 years in the elderly.

drugs.name: Oral glucose
drugs.dose: 15 to 20 g; repeat after 15 minutes if still below 70 mg/dL
drugs.notes: Follow with a meal or snack.

drugs.name: Glucagon
drugs.dose: IM or SC; repeat 0.5 mg if no improvement
drugs.notes: Severe hypoglycaemia when IV glucose is not possible.
